shorts.title: What you will learn: Constructor and destructor order
shorts.hook: The base is always built first.
shorts.script: The base is always built first. Today we learn who is built first. The order matters a lot when classes depend on each other. When you make a derived object, the base part is built first. Then the derived part is built. When the object dies, the order reverses. The derived part goes first, and then the base part. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Constructor and destructor order.

shorts.title: Constructor and destructor order in one minute
shorts.hook: When you make a derived object, the base part is built first.
shorts.script: When you make a derived object, the base part is built first. Then the derived part is built. When the object dies, the order reverses. The derived part goes first, and then the base part. To give arguments to the base constructor, call it in the initializer list. Think of building a house. The foundation comes first, and the roof comes last. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Constructor and destructor order in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The base constructor needs a name.
shorts.script: The base constructor needs a name. The derived constructor takes a name and an age. In the initializer list, we call the base constructor first. Then we set the age. Main passes both values. The output is Moti, three. The program prints Moti and three. The base part is built first. The derived part is built next. Destruction runs in the reverse order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A base with no default constructor
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in constructor and destructor order?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in constructor and destructor order? Bug of the Day. Animal needs a name, but Dog does not give one. The compiler says no matching function for call to Animal. The base part is built first, so the compiler must call a base constructor. Name it in the initializer list. The base part must be built first. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A base with no default constructor.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you trace the order in constructor and destructor order?
shorts.script: Can you trace the order in constructor and destructor order? The base class was always first in line. It said, I was here before you were derived. Write three classes: A, B inherits from A, and C inherits from B. Print a message in each constructor. Predict the order for a C object. Write your answer in the comments. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
